questions.stem: The length of a basic rectangle is exactly 10 cm and its width is 5 cm. What is its total area?
questions.explanation: The formula for the area of a rectangle is Area = Length × Width. Here, Area = 10 cm × 5 cm = 50 sq cm.

questions.stem: The side of a perfect square is exactly 8 cm. What is its total outer perimeter?
questions.explanation: The formula for the perimeter of a square is Perimeter = 4 × Side. Here, Perimeter = 4 × 8 cm = 32 cm.

questions.stem: The total area of a complete circle is 154 sq cm. What is its exact circumference? (Take pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area = πr² = 154. (22/7) × r² = 154. r² = (154 × 7) / 22 = 7 × 7 = 49. So, radius r = 7 cm. Circumference = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 44 cm.

questions.stem: The ratio of the three sides of a triangle is exactly 3:4:5 and its total perimeter is 36 cm. What is the precise area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Let the sides be 3x, 4x, and 5x. Perimeter = 3x + 4x + 5x = 12x = 36. So, x = 3. The sides are 9 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm. Since 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15², this is a right-angled triangle. Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 9 × 12 = 54 sq cm.

questions.stem: If the length of a rectangle is mathematically increased by 20% and its breadth is simultaneously decreased by 10%, what will be the exact percentage change in its overall area?
questions.explanation: Successive percentage change formula is x + y + (xy/100). Here, x = +20 (increase) and y = -10 (decrease). Change = 20 - 10 + (20 × -10)/100 = 10 - 200/100 = 10 - 2 = +8%. The positive sign indicates an 8% increase in area.

questions.stem: A circular wire of exactly radius 42 cm is cut and meticulously bent into the form of a rectangle whose sides are in the precise ratio of 6 : 5. Find the exact length of the smaller side of the rectangle.
questions.explanation: Length of the wire = Circumference of the circle = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 42 = 44 × 6 = 264 cm. This wire forms the rectangle, so Perimeter of rectangle = 264 cm. Let the sides of the rectangle be 6x and 5x. Perimeter = 2(L + B) = 2(6x + 5x) = 2(11x) = 22x. So, 22x = 264 => x = 12. The smaller side = 5x = 5 × 12 = 60 cm.

questions.stem: The total area of a perfect rhombus is exactly 240 sq cm and one of its main diagonals measures exactly 16 cm. Find the total perimeter of the rhombus.
questions.explanation: Area of a rhombus = (1/2) × d1 × d2. 240 = (1/2) × 16 × d2. 240 = 8 × d2 => d2 = 30 cm. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90 degrees). The half-diagonals are 16/2 = 8 cm and 30/2 = 15 cm. These form a right-angled triangle with the side of the rhombus as the hypotenuse. Side² = 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289. So, Side = √289 = 17 cm. Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × 17 = 68 cm.
